message: Sentence-final period after Thai text: delete the period; Thai sentences end without punctuation (D-07).
Period ending a Thai sentence inside the value, or ending a Thai value after a Latin word: separate sentences with one space and drop the period.
Thai digit: write ASCII digits 0-9 (D-04).
Comma between Thai words: Thai separates clauses and list items with one space, with และ / หรือ before the last item.
Comma after Thai text: drop it and separate with one space.
Thai letter directly before a Latin letter, a digit or a {placeholder}: insert one space (ปริมาณ GC, ไฟล์ {name}).
Latin letter, digit, % or {placeholder} directly before a Thai letter: insert one space ({count} ระเบียน, 35% ของ).

regex: ครับ|ค่ะ|กรุณา
message: Polite particle or กรุณา: the UI uses no ครับ / ค่ะ, and "please" is โปรด, at most once per message.

regex: (?<!เ)ท่าน|ข้าพเจ้า|กระผม|ดิฉัน|พวกเรา
message: Pronoun the UI does not use: leave the subject out, or write คุณ for the user and ระบบ for the app.
Tone mark stored before an above vowel or mai taikhu: store the vowel first, then the tone mark (ตั้ง is ต + ั + ้ + ง).
Thai marks in the wrong order, doubled or orphaned: below vowel before the tone mark (ปู่), tone mark before SARA AM (น้ำ), แ not เเ, ำ not ํา, and every mark on a consonant.

regex: ๆ|ๆ[ก-ฮะ-ฺเ-ๅ็-๎]
message: Mai yamok ๆ attaches to the word it repeats and takes one space after it (ต่างๆ ที่).
Question or exclamation mark after Thai: end a question with หรือไม่ and no mark; do not use !
Spacing around ( ) : …: one space before ( and after ) between Thai words; a colon attaches to its label and takes one space after it; … attaches to the word before it.
Letters of another script (Arabic, Devanagari, Lao, Myanmar, Khmer, CJK, kana, Hangul, full-width forms) in a Thai value: a model token leak; rewrite in Thai.
Three periods: write one … (U+2026) attached to the word before it (STYLE §1.2).
ASCII quote in a Thai value: use “ ” (nested ‘ ’).
60 or more Thai characters without a space: put a phrase space where a clause ends so the reader can parse it and the line can wrap.
Leading, trailing or doubled space, or an invisible character (NBSP, ZWSP, ZWNJ, ZWJ, WJ, BOM): use single ordinary spaces only.
